messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — seeing steady resident memory growth on qwen-14b-mqa when rope scaling goes >8k. Repro on dedicated pool after ~45m of mixed chat load. Not a spike, slow climb + KV page churn.
Samir Nikhil: ugh. can you paste the perf traces + kv stats? rough numbers ok.
Alex Chen: pasted a tiny dump, tl;dr: pages allocated kept increasing, gc/sweep runs but freeable pages not reused. Kernel toggles between fast-quant and fallback a bunch.
Maria Gomez: can you run `kv_dump.py --summarize` for that host? also which kernel variant was selected (avx2 vs cuda-fused)?
Alex Chen: attached snippet from host: ```
KV_PAGES.total=1_024_000
KV_PAGES.free=18_400
KV_PAGES.used=1_005_600
sweep.count=42
last_compact=2026-11-02T09:12:11Z
kernel=quant_opt_v2 -> fallback=pad_kernel_slow
batched_avg_size=6
```
Samir Nikhil: batch size 6 is small — odd given our batching heuristic should push to ~12 for chat mix. Are you seeing many short seq requests?
Alex Chen: yes lots of short-turn chats, but we thought batching heuristics would still coalesce. Looks like when kernel fallback happens it disables prefixed KV reuse paths leading to fragmentation.
Jin Park: fwiw we saw similar pattern earlier with llama-mqa on the microbench. Kernel swap can change page alignment assumptions, so old pages become non-contiguous for new allocation layout -> fragmentation. If compactor expects aligned slabs it might skip coalescing.
Maria Gomez: repro steps? I can try an isolated run with synthetic mix. if we hit it, i'll capture `malloc_stats` + `kv_page_map` before/after sweep.
Alex Chen: repro script: https://stash/repro/kv_rope_growth.sh (very small). Steps: 1) set ROPE_SCALE=9000 for qwen variant 2) run mixed chat generator at 120 rps 3) after 30m watch `pmap` and `kv_dump`.
Samir Nikhil: also correlated with a perf regression in nightly: job 2026-11-01-kv-regress flagged by ci-bot. it shows increased p99 latencies and a small throughput drop when kernel selector enabled quant_opt_v2.
ci-bot: Perf alert: job=2026-11-01-kv-regress, delta_p99=+18ms, delta_throughput=-3.5%. See https://ci/reports/2026-11-01-kv-regress
Jin Park: my theory: quant_opt_v2 introduces a different slab size for cached KV entries when GQA->MQA folding happens. On rope scale >8k, KV key lengths push into a different bucket, and fallback kernels don't reuse those buckets. Combined with our lazy sweep (interval 10m) results in slow growth.
Maria Gomez: sounds plausible. quick mitigation — bump compaction frequency and force a full compact after rollout for affected pools. that should regain reuse. Want me to open a temporary rollout?
Alex Chen: please. Can we also add a micro-benchmark that toggles kernel selection rapidly to simulate the churn? If we can reproduce in CI we can test compactor changes.
Samir Nikhil: i'll add a test to perf-suite: kv_kernel_churn_test. It will flip kernel_selector every N requests and run 1M tokens.
Jin Park: long-term fix: make compactor consider cross-kernel bucket coalescing or make kernel ABI preserve page slab shapes. I'll prototype a compat layer that maps old slab headers to new layout.
Alex Chen: agreed. For immediate triage: Maria increase compaction to 2m for that dedicated pool, Samir add the churn test, Jin start a prototype. I'll collect more heap snapshots and attach them to the issue.
Maria Gomez: on it :thumbsup:
Samir Nikhil: ETA for the perf test push ~2 hours.
Jin Park: prototype plan posted in #eng-runtime PR later today.
Alex Chen: thanks all. keeping this thread as the triage channel. I'll update with snapshots when available.
